metadata.name: Corrected Phenytoin Level (Winter-Tozer Equation)
metadata.summary: Estimates total phenytoin equivalent in hypoalbuminemia and/or end-stage renal disease.
clinical_pearls: Winter-Tozer is an approximation; directly measure free (unbound) phenytoin whenever available in ICU, pregnancy, or valproate co-therapy.

Phenytoin has a narrow therapeutic window and is ~90% protein-bound; standard lab assays measure total phenytoin, whereas unbound phenytoin crosses the blood-brain barrier and exerts pharmacologic activity.

Pitfall — ICU, trauma, and displacing drugs: Winter-Tozer and derivative equations show variable predictive performance in neuro-ICU, trauma, and hypoalbuminemic elderly patients (Kane et al., 2013; Kiang & Ensom, 2016), and cannot account for protein-binding displacement by valproate, salicylates, or hyperbilirubinemia.

interpretation.label: Subtherapeutic (< 10 mcg/mL)
interpretation.summary: Corrected level below standard 10–20 mcg/mL reference range.

interpretation.label: Therapeutic Range (10–20 mcg/mL)
interpretation.summary: Within standard total phenytoin therapeutic window.

interpretation.label: Supratherapeutic (20.1–30 mcg/mL)
interpretation.summary: Elevated; assess for nystagmus, ataxia, or sedation.

interpretation.label: Toxic Range (> 30 mcg/mL)
interpretation.summary: High risk of CNS toxicity; hold dose and obtain free phenytoin level.

assessment_guides.title: When Winter-Tozer Underperforms
bedside_steps: Use measured total phenytoin and serum albumin drawn on the same day.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Valproate, salicylates, and hyperbilirubinemia displace phenytoin from albumin independently of albumin concentration—order a free phenytoin level (target 1–2 mcg/mL) in these settings.
